forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Enfield secures 3% pension contribution saving from April
news_drafts.lead: Enfield Council will reduce its employer pension contributions by 3% from April 2026 following an independent financial assessment, known as an actuarial valuation, of the Enfield Pension Fund. The fund's net assets reached £1.71bn at 31 March 2026, having grown by £301m over the previous five years, confirming the improved funding position. However, the fund is now experiencing negative cashflow of approximately £2.0m annually, with pension benefit payments exceeding contribution income, reflecting the aging membership base and requiring active liquidity management.

findings.headline: Academy conversions could disrupt schools capital programme as DfE grants are restricted to maintained schools
findings.detail: The council identifies a risk that if schools convert to academy status, grant funding for capital works becomes unavailable. Where planned works for a converting school have not yet been committed (contracts not yet awarded), the programme may need to be varied in-year, with alternative priority projects added under delegated authority to the Executive Director of People.
findings.matters: Unplanned academy conversions could force last-minute programme revision, delay maintenance work, or require reprioritization away from planned condition or SEND provision improvements.
findings.figures: No data on likelihood or timing of conversions
findings.quote: In the event that schools convert to academy status, the agreed programme may need to be varied in-year where planned works have not yet been committed, as grant funding is restricted to maintained schools.

findings.headline: Construction market volatility poses risk to delivery against budgets estimated from 2022/23 condition surveys
findings.detail: The council acknowledges that tender prices for capital works may significantly exceed budgets estimated from condition surveys. Projects will be delivered through staged process with cost checks at each stage to adjust scope if necessary to remain within budget. Where costs exceed estimates, approved contingency sums may need to be used to supplement project budgets to enable completion.
findings.matters: Rising construction costs could force value-engineering or scope reduction on maintenance projects, potentially compromising the condition backlog reduction strategy or drawing down contingency reserves.
findings.figures: Contingency budgets £0.55m (2026/27) and £0.60m (2027/28); baseline cost estimates from 2022/23 surveys
findings.quote: Given the volatility of the construction market, tender prices may significantly exceed budgets estimated from condition surveys. Projects will therefore be delivered through a staged process, with cost checks at each stage to allow the scope to be adjusted, where feasible, to remain within available budgets.

findings.headline: Schools capital programme to be funded entirely from DfE grants and capital receipts, with no call on council general fund
findings.detail: The entire 2026/27-2029/30 programme is funded from ring-fenced DfE grants (Schools Capital Allocation, Basic Needs Grant, High Needs Grant), capital receipts from caretaker property sales, and external funding (Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme, Greater London Authority). The council explicitly confirms no call on general fund resources, meaning capital investment does not draw on reserves.
findings.matters: While positive for general fund finances, it indicates tight constraint within available grant-funded resources with no flexibility to address emerging pressures beyond the allocated envelope.
findings.figures: Total DfE grants available 2026/27: £57.59m (£46.20m brought forward + £11.39m received/expected); external PSDS funding £18m (not included in capital programme)
findings.quote: This ambitious programme is supported through the use of ring-fenced capital grants, external funding and capital receipts with no call made on the Councils resources.

findings.headline: Electrical and mechanical building services at schools have exceeded design life; 10-year replacement programme emerging
findings.detail: Detailed surveys of electrical and mechanical services commissioned in 2026/27 show that much of the building services infrastructure has exceeded its design life and requires replacement over the next decade. Major works include replacement of electrical mains and distribution cabling, light fittings, hot and cold-water pipework, heating pipework, radiators, boilers and hot water systems. Final survey reports are due later in 2026 to inform future programming; urgent works are being included in the current programme.
findings.matters: Early indication that substantial capital investment beyond the £100m condition backlog will be needed across the next decade, materially increasing total capital demand.
findings.figures: 10-year replacement programme, but specific cost estimates not yet finalised; final reports due later in 2026
findings.quote: During 2026/27, detailed surveys of electrical and mechanical services in schools have been progressed to supplement the high-level condition findings. Early indications suggest that much of the building services infrastructure has exceeded its design life and will need to be replaced through a 10-year programme.

findings.headline: Addison House fire-damaged in July 2026, withdrawn from SEN programme with insurance claim ongoing
findings.detail: A vacant education building at Addison House was severely fire damaged in July 2026. The land and buildings have been made safe and secured, with insurance investigations ongoing to assess the cause. The council has decided not to develop Special Educational Needs provision on this site, concluding the capital investment required would be significant but deliver too few SEN places for value for money. The site is to be added to the disposals programme.
findings.matters: Loss of a planned SEN provision site means the council must identify alternative locations to meet SEND reform commitments; the insurance outcome will determine whether there is recovery to offset other capital pressures.
findings.figures: No financial figures provided for fire damage or insurance claim
findings.quote: Earlier in July, this vacant building was severely fire damaged, the land and buildings have been made safe and secure. Insurance investigations are ongoing to assess the cause of the fire and next steps.
